qa.q: What is the Start Here page?
qa.a: It's the front door to the C2A2 explorer. It orients newcomers and links out to the fifteen angles on what C2A2 is, the review cards, the Summa commentary, and the Sociogram.

qa.q: Where should I begin if I'm new?
qa.a: Start Here. From there you can jump to any of the main tools, or read the fifteen framings of what the project is.

qa.q: How do I get back to the beginning?
qa.a: Click the Start Here tab in the top bar any time — it's always there.

qa.q: What can I do from the Start Here page?
qa.a: Jump straight into any main tool, or open the fifteen framings of what C2A2 is, the review cards, and the Summa commentary.
Fifteen different framings of what the project is — no single one tells the whole story, but together they describe it.
A record of the proposals and decisions behind what's been added to the wiki — the project's paper trail.

qa.q: Is Start Here different from the Community Explorer?
qa.a: Yes. Start Here is the orientation page; the Community Explorer is a separate tool that maps real-world communities.
A force-directed graph of 156 curated real-world communities across eight types, from contemplative to scientific-frontier. Communities working on kindred problems sit close together.

qa.q: What do the edges mean here?
qa.a: They're PRS similarity — communities with related problems, resources, and solutions are linked and pulled near each other.

qa.q: How do I explore a community?
qa.a: Click a node to read its Problem-Resource-Solution story, or click an edge to compare the two communities it connects. You can also filter by type or isolate the exemplary set.

qa.q: How does this relate to the Cards view?
qa.a: These 156 are the quality-curated subset. The Cards sub-tab holds the full directory of over a thousand communities.

qa.q: What are the eight community types?
qa.a: Tradition-Constituted Enquiry, Practice, Contemplative, Civic, Scientific Frontier, Interdisciplinary Synthesis, Local, and Professional Guilds.

qa.q: What does isolating the exemplary set do?
qa.a: It filters the graph down to the highest-quality communities so you can focus on the strongest examples.

qa.q: Why do some communities sit close together?
qa.a: Because they score as similar on Problem-Resource-Solution terms — they're tackling kindred problems.

qa.q: How many communities are in the curated graph?
qa.a: 156, hand-curated across the eight types. The larger raw directory lives in the Cards view.
A scaffold for the four levels of dialogue C2A2 cares about: within one mind, within a small group, between traditions, and between whole systems of thought.
Level one is intrapersonal integration, level two is small-group tradition, level three is inter-tradition dialogue, and level four is meta-traditional encounter.

qa.q: What is the Road Ahead section?
qa.a: It renders the project's development pathways live from the single source, so you can see where C2A2 is heading and what's on the demo critical path.
Intrapersonal integration — dialogue within a single mind or agent.
Meta-traditional encounter — dialogue between whole systems of thought.
No, it's an actively developing scaffold — the shape of what's coming, not the final architecture.

qa.q: Where does the Road Ahead come from?
qa.a: It renders live from the project's single-source pathways index, so it always reflects the current plan.
A force-directed graph of the whole RC Wiki — over sixteen hundred nodes for wiki articles, connected by wikilinks, mentions, and shared references.

qa.q: How do I read a specific article?
qa.a: Click any node and its article opens in the side panel. Click an edge to see both articles it connects.

qa.q: Can I focus on one thinker?
qa.a: Yes — use the tradition and category filters on the left to isolate a thinker's conceptual neighborhood, or just ask me to show it.

qa.q: What do the edge controls do?
qa.a: They let you show or hide link types and adjust how strongly connected nodes attract each other.

qa.q: How many nodes are in the Sociogram?
qa.a: Over sixteen hundred, one for each wiki article, connected by thousands of links.

qa.q: What do the edge types mean?
qa.a: They distinguish wikilinks, mentions, and shared references, and whether a link crosses categories or stays within one.
A checkbox that isolates one thinker's articles — Levin, Friston, Hoffman, and so on — so you can see their neighborhood.
Groupings like Master, Architecture, Agents, and others that organize the wiki by role rather than by thinker.

qa.q: Can I hold the layout still?
qa.a: Yes — use Hold Forces to freeze the graph, and Fit All to recenter everything in view.
A 3D connectome of the C2A2 traditions. Each node is a Problem-Resource-Solution narrative — a small model of a problem, its resource, and its solution.
Shared resources, plus the synergistic coils that bridge one tradition to another. Read it as rival master sciences emerging.

qa.q: How do I move around it?
qa.a: Rotate and zoom with your mouse to explore the structure from any angle.
A small model of a tradition's thinking: a problem it faces, the resource it brings, and the solution that follows.
Links where one tradition's solution answers another tradition's problem — the bridges between master sciences.
So you can rotate and zoom through the connections and see structure that a flat graph would flatten out.
The idea that each tradition is growing into a full account of reality, and the connectome shows them emerging side by side.
A live map of the autonomous agents running C2A2 — the daily synthesis batch, QC sweep, commentary reviewer, nightly verification, and wiki update agents.

qa.q: What does it show for each agent?
qa.a: Each agent's last run time, its output status, and its task schedule.

qa.q: How do I see what's running now?
qa.a: Open the Agent Map and check the last-run and status columns — that's the current state of the swarm.
The daily synthesis batch, a QC sweep, the commentary reviewer, nightly verification, and the wiki update agents.

qa.q: What does the QC sweep do?
qa.a: It checks the day's output for quality problems before they land in the wiki.

qa.q: How do I tell if an agent failed?
qa.a: Check its status and last-run time on the map — a stale run or an error status flags a problem.
An agent that reviews annotation and commentary content for the education tools.
The temporal pulse of the agent swarm, built from run telemetry and the vault's git history. It treats the human-plus-AI system's metabolism as something you can measure.
A per-agent raster of runs over time, a waveform of the system's daily pulse, and a returned-versus-sent tokens chart.
A live measure of useful output — wikilinks, files, and PRS triplets produced per day, drawn from the vault's git history.
A per-agent timeline of runs, where each mark's size reflects an amplitude you choose, like tokens or duration.
The system's daily pulse, stacked by category or shown on a log axis, so you can see the rhythm of the swarm.
How much the agents produce relative to what they consume — a rough efficiency signal.
The project pathway behind this view: treating the human-plus-AI system's metabolism as something measurable.
The Summa 2026 curriculum dashboard. It tracks daily synthesis progress through Austin Habash's 308-episode podcast series.
Which days have been synthesized, where the coverage gaps are, and the current continuous-day high-water mark.

qa.q: How does it connect to the wiki?
qa.a: Each synthesis ties a specific episode's content back to the RC Wiki thinker network.
Austin Habash's Summa 2026 series — a 308-episode run being synthesized day by day.
308, and the dashboard tracks how many have been synthesized so far.

qa.q: What is the continuous-day high-water mark?
qa.a: The longest unbroken streak of days that have been synthesized without a gap.
A day in the series that hasn't been synthesized yet — the dashboard shows where those are.
A structured tool for comparing the thinker traditions against each other — where they converge, where they clash, and where one answers another's open question.
It's the detector half of C2A2 at work: instrumenting what happens when traditions meet, rather than just hoping a good conversation occurs.
Pick the traditions you want to compare and read across their problems and solutions. Ask me and I can open it for you.

qa.q: What questions does Inter-Tradition Study answer?
qa.a: Where the traditions converge, where they clash, and where one tradition resolves another's open problem.

qa.q: How is it different from the Sociogram?
qa.a: The Sociogram maps the whole wiki; this tool focuses on structured comparison between traditions.

qa.q: What does the detector half mean?
qa.a: It instruments what happens when traditions meet, rather than leaving it to chance — C2A2's measurement side.
Yes — surfacing tension between traditions is as much the point as finding agreement.

qa.q: What is the RC Document Explorer?
qa.a: A pedagogical explorer for the 471-page Resurrecting Civility tome — the founding research dialogue behind the whole C2A2 thinker network.
Contents, with 679 hyperlinked sections; Thinkers, nine research programs each with a summary and its PRS triplets; and Solved, the full PRS table with cross-tradition coil detection.
Yes — the chat pane searches by keyword, or answers semantically through the shared C2A2 broker, no key needed.
The 471-page pilot tome and founding research dialogue behind the whole C2A2 thinker network.
The full Problem-Resource-Solution table, with detection of coils where a solution answers a problem across traditions.

qa.q: How many thinkers does it cover?
qa.a: Nine research programs, each with a summary and its own set of PRS triplets.

qa.q: How do I jump to a source page?
qa.a: Click any problem, resource, or solution and it takes you to its page; use Return to come back.
A teachable map of physics from Newton to today, applying the same Problem-Resource-Solution lens to a curriculum instead of a research dialogue.
75 undergraduate concepts with formulas and linked demos and simulations, six physicists each with summaries and triplets, and a progress chart of problems solved over time.

qa.q: Can I change how much detail it shows?
qa.a: Yes — switch between Student and Instructor mode at the top right to change the depth on each card.

qa.q: Does the assistant need a key?
qa.a: No. Ask it a physics question and it runs on the shared C2A2 pipeline, or uncheck Ask AI for plain keyword search.

qa.q: How many physics concepts are included?
qa.a: 75 undergraduate concepts across six topic areas, each with formulas and links to a demo and a simulation.

qa.q: What's the difference between Student and Instructor mode?
qa.a: It changes how much depth each card shows — a lighter view for students, a fuller one for instructors.

qa.q: What does the Progress view show?
qa.a: A count of problems solved and resources introduced at each stage — a quantified history of progress in physics.

qa.q: How many physicists does it cover?
qa.a: Six, each with a short summary and two sets of triplets drawn from their work.
An annotated-reading explorer for MacIntyre's Three Rival Versions of Moral Enquiry — his 1988 Gifford Lectures — with 1,819 annotations across 156 scanned pages.
The book's twelve structural divisions as chapter nodes, with satellites for Tom Loughran's marginal commentary, PRS triplets, and companion views from Eleonore Stump and N. T. Wright.

qa.q: How do I read a chapter?
qa.a: Click a chapter to walk its pages in the right panel; the OCR pane highlights where each annotation anchors in the text.
Alasdair MacIntyre — it's his 1988 Gifford Lectures, published by Notre Dame Press in 1990.
1,819 annotations across 156 scanned pages.
Tom Loughran's marginal notes and PRS triplets, plus companion perspectives from Eleonore Stump and N. T. Wright.
The annotated scan runs through Chapter Eight; Chapters Nine and Ten are structural placeholders.
A Karpathy-style compiled wiki over fast-moving AI developments, reframed for community AI education. Raw sources stay immutable while runs summarize, tag, and score them.
It loads a static digest snapshot of the latest developments, so the tab works on GitHub Pages with no live backend.

qa.q: Can I tune what I see?
qa.a: Yes — set a preference lens, and a magic-link sign-in syncs it across your devices.

qa.q: What does the AI Heartbeat track?
qa.a: Fast-moving AI developments, compiled Karpathy-style and reframed for community AI education.
Your chosen viewpoint that shapes how developments are framed and ranked for you.
A magic-link sign-in syncs your lens and preferences across your devices.

qa.q: Is the Heartbeat live or a snapshot?
qa.a: The Pulse view loads a static digest snapshot, so it works on GitHub Pages with no live backend.

qa.q: What is the Community Cards view?
qa.a: A faceted directory of over a thousand real-world communities — a bulk web import plus the 156 curated ones. Each carries a Problem-Resource-Solution triplet.

qa.q: How do I search the cards?
qa.a: Filter by type, subtype, country, or source, or just ask in plain language — the built-in engine answers from the dataset.
It's under construction and was seeded from public web pages without the communities' express consent, so treat it as a working directory, not a finished one.

qa.q: How many communities are in the Cards directory?
qa.a: Over a thousand — a bulk web import plus the 156 curated ones that carry the richer taxonomy.
Yes, by type, subtype, country, or source — or just ask in plain language and the built-in engine answers from the data.

qa.q: Where did the cards data come from?
qa.a: It was seeded from publicly available web pages, so treat it as a working directory under construction, not a vetted list.
A community's Problem-Resource-Solution triplet plus a short summary of its organizing principle.
